demoCaption: Default replies with sample names and numbers. Your saved messages can differ.
metaDesc: Build a Twitch death counter with ItsBagelBot custom counters. Track a channel total or per-viewer counts, update from chat, and reset between runs.
title: Keep the count through every attempt.
lead: Use a custom counter as your Twitch death counter. Create a channel total called deaths, add to it from moderator chat, and reset it for the next run. Counters also support separate values per viewer, per command, or per viewer and command.
howTitle: Create a counter for your next run.
step1Desc: Add a channel counter named deaths in Counters, or use !counter create deaths with Loyalty enabled. Omitting the scope in chat creates a channel counter.
step2Desc: A moderator can type !counter add deaths 1. Use !counter deaths to read the value. Custom command responses and channel-point rewards can also update counters when configured.
step3Desc: Use !counter reset deaths to return the channel total to zero. !counter set deaths 12 replaces the current value with a chosen number.
tblNote: The catalog exposes one !counter command family. Its usage covers create, add, set, reset, delete, list and reading a named counter. These chat controls are moderator-only and run through the Loyalty module.
demoTitle: Create deaths, then add the first one.
listTitle: Choose what each value belongs to.
item1Desc: A channel counter holds one shared value. It suits a death count for the streamer or a total of wins during a challenge.
item2Desc: A viewer counter keeps separate values for each viewer. Create one with !counter create hugs user, then use a configured command or reward to count for its caller.
item3Desc: A command counter separates values by command. The viewer-and-command scope separates them by both the viewer and the command.
item4Desc: Counters can be created and adjusted in the dashboard as well as from chat. Use the scope that matches the total you want to keep.
limitsNote: A custom death counter changes when you or a configured command or reward updates it. Counting is manual or configured; creating the counter does not detect deaths in a game.
prereq1: Connect ItsBagelBot to your Twitch channel and create a custom counter in Counters.
prereq2: Enable Loyalty for !counter chat controls, and use the streamer or a moderator account to run them.
faqQ1: How do I add a Twitch death counter?
faqA1: Create a channel counter named deaths in the dashboard. With Loyalty enabled, a moderator can instead type !counter create deaths, then !counter add deaths 1 for each death.
faqQ2: Does the bot automatically detect deaths?
faqA2: A custom counter records updates you send to it. Add from chat, adjust in the dashboard, or configure a command response or channel-point reward to update it.
faqA3: !counter is moderator-only. To let viewers interact with a count, configure a custom command or channel-point reward with the permissions and counter behavior you want.
faqQ4: How do I reset the death count?
faqA4: For the channel counter deaths, use !counter reset deaths. To correct a total instead, use !counter set deaths followed by the replacement number.
faqQ5: Can I keep a separate count for each viewer?
faqA5: Yes. Use the viewer scope, called user when creating it from chat. Channel scope shares one total; viewer scope keeps a separate value for each viewer. Command and viewer-and-command scopes are also supported.
ctaTitle: Set up the count before your next run.
